title: The literalist convergence
statement: Independent readers with different starting points, methods, and stakes — Jean Sendy (1963, the first finished statement, with a falsifiable lunar wager he lost), Mauro Biglino (a publisher-sanctioned interlinear translator whose literalism outlived his commission), and Paul Wallis (a serving Anglican archdeacon reading from inside the church) — arrived at plural, physical, mortal Elohim readings of the same Hebrew texts; the corpus registers the convergence as significant reception evidence while carrying in full the objection that a shared modern idiom, not a shared correct referent, may drive it.

includes: The three documented cases at their own strength: Sendy's 1963 statement and its explicit falsifiable wager (lunar installations, staked on Apollo — and lost, a failure the corpus treats as the model of honest staking rather than an embarrassment to bury); Biglino's interlinear-translation path into literalism; Wallis's intra-church path (whose serpent-case discipline woh-claim-0022 already carries)
The independence audit: different decades, confessions, languages, and professional stakes — the features that make the convergence more than one milieu talking to itself

The registration discipline: convergence is registered as reception evidence for the reading's availability in the texts, never as demonstration of its truth; the structure-severed-from-etymology rule applies to every case
excludes: Any claim that convergence demonstrates correctness; the artifact objection is the standing default
Enrollment of the readers in the framework; Sendy, Biglino, and Wallis hold their own positions, preserved in their own voices
Extension to the ancient-astronaut genre generally (Sitchin, von Daniken); the record's cases are literalist readers of the Hebrew text, and the genre's speculative wing is outside it
Sendy's lost wager as evidence against the framework's own claims; the corpus's claims stake themselves on their own recorded triggers, not on his

source_references.locator: The 1963 statement and the lunar wager
The interlinear-derived literalism and its break with the commission
The intra-church reading (the serpent-case engagement carried by woh-claim-0022)

alternatives.statement: Space-age readers converge on space-age readings; the idiom of the era, not the texts' referent, drives the convergence.
Convergent readers are counted; divergent literalists are not — the sample is survivorship.
The three methods differ enough that the shared conclusion may be the only shared thing; convergence of conclusions without convergence of method is weak evidence.

revision_triggers: A documented divergent-literalist census materially changes the selection picture.
Case-level review (the readers' works are wantlist items) changes a case's characterization.
Public prose begins citing convergence as demonstration or enrolling the readers, both of which this record excludes.
